title: Synthetic cohort canary recipes and run notes
content:
Purpose and scope

This note captures a set of pragmatic "recipes" for running small synthetic-cohort canaries and A/B slices for LLM features. Aim: exercise end-to-end routing, billing/telemetry integration, and quality signal detection before opening to organic traffic. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — a lab notebook for cross-functional teams (product, SRE, ML infra, observations).

What is a synthetic cohort canary (short)
- A short-lived traffic slice populated with generated or replayed requests that mimic target cohorts (e.g., search queries, chat prompts, reranker batches).
- Purpose: force predictable traffic patterns, amplify rare failure modes, validate model variants and routing fallbacks, and exercise telemetry/alerting.

Personas and responsibilities
- Feature owner (Product): defines hypothesis and guardrail metrics.
- Steward (Ops/Oncall): runs traffic generator, monitors signals, executes roll-forward/rollback.
- ML owner (Applied ML): provides eval prompts and quality heuristics.
- Infra (Serving/runtime): ensures model variants and capacity routing are ready.
- Observability/Console: ensures dashboards and alert rules are live.

High-level hypothesis template
- H0: New model variant V2 yields no regression in quality and reduces token cost by >=12% for the target cohort.
- Primary metric: human-pass rate on critical prompt set (synthetic->human eval fallback).
- Secondary metrics: P95 latency, token-cost-per-response, failure-rate (5xx), hallucination-flag-rate (automated heuristic).

Quick recipe: small synthetic canary (20–30 minutes)
1) Build cohort: choose 250–1,000 seed prompts that represent the cohort distribution (mix short/long, chain-of-thought, edge-case intents).
2) Traffic profile: emulate real qps but scaled to 3–5qps for 20 minutes (keeps downstream queues small, still exercises batching).
3) Sampling weights: 60% happy-path, 25% ambiguous prompts, 15% adversarial/edge prompts.
4) Model mapping: route 100% of synthetic cohort to candidate variant; ensure a simultaneous 0% organic to candidate.
5) Observability: enable token-level breakdown, P50/P95, error traces, embedding-similarity checks, and a small human review cohort (5 prompts every 5m).
6) Success gate: no increase >1.5x in hallucination-flag-rate and P95 latency within 10% of baseline for the 20min window.

Longer canary (micro-exposure with ramping)
- Duration: 6–12 hours. Purpose: catch diurnal and batch-scheduling interactions.
- Start 10% synthetic + 0% organic, then add 10% organic after first 2 hours if signals stable.
- Ramp rule: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 6 hours; pause/reroll at each step if any guardrail breaches.

A/B slice experiment recipe (product-facing)
- Use for feature conversions, UX changes, or quality vs cost trade-offs.
- Randomize at user-id or session-id boundary, not request-level.
- Minimum sample size calc: use baseline conversion and desired detectable delta; default to 20k impressions per arm for language feature launches.
- Tie experiment to per-prompt quality checks (BLEU/ROUGE not reliable for chat; prefer semantic-sim and specific behavior flags).

Synthetic traffic generation notes
- Replayer vs generator: replayer uses production traces (best for fidelity); generator mixes templated prompts to force edge coverage.
- Rate shaping: add jitter to avoid pathological batching at exact intervals. Introduce 15–30% randomness in inter-arrival times.
- Prefix caching: include both cache-hit and cache-miss patterns to exercise KV cache behavior.

Telemetry and signal recipes (must-haves)
- Latency: P50, P95, P99 token generation time by model variant and route.
- Cost: tokens consumed per response and projected per-million-token cost.
- Quality proxies: automated hallucination heuristic, contradiction checks, hallucination-flag-rate, semantic-similarity to expected reference (avg), rerank-score change distribution.
- Stability: 5xx rate, 4xx rate, retry counts, queue length.
- User-visible regression: automated human pass/fail sample every X minutes.

Fail-open / fail-closed design patterns
- Short latency budget features: prefer fail-open to simpler fallback model variant with narrower context window.
- Safety-sensitive features: default to fail-closed and route to a human-review queue or blocking UX.
- Routing fallback sequence example: V2 -> V1-quantized -> V1-cached -> V0-legacy. Each fallback has a explicit SLO and token-cost upper bound.

Guardrails and thresholds (suggested starting points)
- P95 latency: +15% over baseline -> investigate; +35% -> rollback.
- 5xx errors: >0.5% sustained for 10 minutes -> pause ramp.
- Hallucination-flag-rate: >2x baseline or >4% absolute -> pause and escalate ML owner.
- Token-cost-per-response: >25% higher for sustained 30m -> evaluate cost/quality trade-off.

War-room checklist (quick)
- Before start: health of model artifacts in catalog, canary route exists, dashboard links open, quicklink to oncall rotation, traffic generator ready with seed set.
- T0 (start): snapshot baseline metrics, start generator, tag experiment run id in traces.
- T+5m: validate P50 within expected band and confirm traces arrive at console.
- T+15m: sample human review and confirm no systemic semantic regressions.
- T+30m: decision point — proceed, pause, or rollback. Use majority of lead signals (quality + infra).
- Rollback steps: disable canary route, revert routing to baseline, stop traffic generator, run postmortem ticket template.

Common failure modes observed in lab runs
- Synthetic prompts over-represent adversarial patterns leading to false positives. Fix: calibrate sampling weights to mirror organic distribution better.
- Batching artifacts: fixed-interval generators may create unrealistic large batches. Fix: add jitter and mix-in low-rate steady stream.
- Telemetry gaps: missing token-level breakdown if telemetry sampling disabled at the model node. Fix: ensure sampling flag enabled before run.

Mini templates (copy-paste into wip run ticket)
- Run title: "synthetic-cohort-canary-<feature>-<date>"
- Hypothesis: <short hypothesis>
- Seed set id: <s3://... or internal id>
- Duration: <min>
- Traffic shape: <qps, jitter>
- Observability links: <dashboard>, <traces>, <alerts>

Open questions / experiments to try next
- Automated prompt stratification: can we auto-generate a weighted seed set from production traces while preserving PII?
- Adaptive sampling: increase adversarial fraction if early heuristics detect instability.
- Synthetic user flows for multi-turn contexts: how to best simulate session-level context and KV cache warmups?

Notes to self (scratchpad)
- Priya wants a short demo for sales engineering that uses the 20m recipe; aim to have a canned seed set and 1-click generator by next sprint.
- Diego to check that rollout metadata tags propagate to billing and Console cost widgets.
- Add a tiny dashboard that shows sample human verdicts in-line with model metrics.

References and appendices
- See linked Confluence page for glossary and signal definitions.
- Keep experiment ticket with screenshots and sample traces.

End of notebook.
